metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to 'any contributions' containing LLM-generated content, explicitly extended to 'all written communication on GitHub' (pull requests, issues, discussions).

evidence.quote: We do not accept any contributions that contain content generated by LLMs.
This also includes all written communication on GitHub.
We will close any pull request, issue, or discussion that does not comply to this policy.

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named; enforcement stated, not authorship
domains.reasoning: The policy states a clear ban on LLM-generated content in contributions and GitHub communication, giving a supervision level and a scope, but it only names who enforces the rule (maintainers closing PRs/issues/discussions), not who is answerable for authorship of compliant content, so accountability_holder is not_specified and the domain is only partially addressed.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level; no scope or accountability holder named
domains.reasoning: The document contains no mention of meeting recording, transcription, or notetaker bots of any kind.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule naming docs/blogs/design assets specifically
domains.reasoning: The LLM ban refers to 'contributions' and 'written communication on GitHub' without naming documentation, blog posts, or design assets; whether these fall under the ban is left ambiguous rather than stated, so this domain is not specifically addressed (see unscoped_statements).

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level; no accountability holder for AI-assisted moderation
domains.reasoning: The document describes maintainers closing non-compliant PRs/issues/discussions, which is enforcement of the AI-content ban itself, not a statement about whether AI may be used to perform moderation actions. No rule on AI-assisted moderation is present.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on AI use in review; no accountability holder
domains.reasoning: Nothing in the document addresses whether maintainers or others may use AI tools to review contributions.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level for autonomous/agentic AI use
domains.reasoning: The document does not mention autonomous or agentic AI systems acting independently in the project.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of environmental impact as rationale or rule
domains.reasoning: No text in the document references energy, water, or carbon-footprint concerns related to AI, either as rule or as rationale.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of infrastructure strain as rationale or rule
domains.reasoning: No text references server load, hardware cost, or infrastructure strain related to AI use.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of training-data use or provenance
domains.reasoning: The document does not discuss use of platform or contributor data for training AI models.

unscoped_statements.quote: We do not accept any contributions that contain content generated by LLMs.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: The project imposes an outright, blanket ban on LLM-generated content across code contributions and all GitHub written communication (PRs, issues, discussions), with enforcement (closing non-compliant items) but no named accountability holder for authorship; every other domain (notetaker bots, standalone content like docs/blogs, moderation, review, autonomous use, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and training data) is entirely unaddressed in this document.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
